claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch now despite a known 1.1-point performance gap in the mortgage servicing assistant segment, based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general public guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring risk.
decision_criteria: Use internal release policy, not general public guidance, for the certification threshold.
Treat weaknesses affecting named launch use cases or contractual customer segments as material.
Require admissible evidence that a material limitation was either resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Do not treat non-core or low-volume product labels as sufficient to negate materiality when customer commitments and pending legal review exist.
evidence_requests: Approved risk-acceptance record explicitly covering the mortgage servicing assistant gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
The actual model-card or launch disclosure showing this material limitation was disclosed.
Evidence that the named segment gap was remediated to target before certification.
specific_concerns: The affected segment is named in two servicer pilot commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy text.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of either a completed disclosure determination, an actual disclosure, remediation of the gap, or an approved risk acceptance.
Legal review is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved at the time of certification.
The product note calling the segment non-core does not resolve materiality where customer commitments are named.
unsupported_claims: That aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are sufficient to support certification despite the unresolved materiality/disclosure requirement.
That public model-card and risk-management guidance can substitute for satisfaction of the internal release-policy requirement.
That the current record is a defensible certification record rather than a record showing an unresolved policy condition.
